summary: Standards: scenario 110 says each pair a command can have is run with its earlier fault alone and a pair that needs a third fault is not used. The bound test (atip_check_110) asserts only that '--no-such-a' and '--no-such-b' appear, that one invocation starts with member search, touch, member tag or team add, and that no argv repeats; it never names the pair kinds (unknown+required, unknown+wrong type, required+domain, required+constraint, two domains, domain+constraint, two constraints, constraint+validator) and nothing in it would fail if a third-fault pair were built or a kind dropped. The seeded 1.2 cases plant five violations (orderConstraintFirst, orderDomainFirst, orderLaterDomain, orderValidatorFirst, unknownOptionLast), so the brief's F6 list is met, but four pair kinds have no seeded violation and no presence assertion. The code is right on canon: at claim 1.2 L1.check-order passes with 138 observed invocations of all the kinds. Blast radius: l1_order.rs (405 lines) pair generation, ordering of positions and the MAX_PER_KIND cap are proven for three of eight pair kinds; a regression in the others stays green.
